title: SUMO behavioural-capture run configuration
description: 12_Operator_Control_Surface.md §3-§6. Positions are in CARLA's frame: metres, x east, y south.

run_configuration_version.description: The version of this schema the document is written against.

mode.description: Which authority drives the world. A scenario package implies sumo_driven_playback, the only mode this front end runs; the traffic-manager path is run_SCTMV.py.

caller.description: attended: a person reads the launch echo and adjudicates warnings at the terminal. unattended: warnings are adjudicated in advance by on_warning, and result_path is required. Recorded, because a corpus whose warnings a file adjudicated is not one a person watched.

caller_label.description: An opaque label the caller recognises its own run by. Recorded and never interpreted.

scenario_package.description: The compiled scenario: a scenario id (found as <id>/<id>.lock.json under paths.scenario_root), a scenario package directory, or its .lock.json. A capture binds a compiled scenario; it never compiles one.

world_package.description: The .cwp the world was built as. Unset, it is the package the scenario lock names, under paths.world_package_root. Its contents are bound, never overridden.

result_path.description: Where the run result is written, outside the capture root. Unset, it is <paths.runs_root>/<session id>/run.result.json; required under caller unattended. The resolution report, the lock and the replayable effective configuration are written beside it.

write_headroom_floor_s.description: Captured seconds of free disk below which the run stops itself cleanly, closed_by write_headroom. The one bound the tool imposes on a run.

monitor.description: The live monitor: a panel on a terminal, a log line every few seconds otherwise.

collision_detail.description: What the run prints about collisions. off: their count, in the session's report. on: every collision as it ends, and every collision and every collision warning SUMO wrote in the session's report. Printing only: the record of collisions is kept in full either way, and nothing about the traffic or the truth depends on it.

on_warning.description: The adjudication of a warning, by code, made in advance: proceed or refuse. Under caller unattended every warning raised must have one.

expect.description: What the caller believes a field or a launch-echo value resolves to, by path. A value is compared for equality; {"at_most": x} or {"at_least": x} bounds a number. An expectation never supplies a value; a failed one refuses the launch.

window.description: Which simulated time to render: a window the scenario declares, by id; '<begin_s>:<end_s>'; or '<begin_s>:' with no end, which runs to the scenario's end unless the caller stops it first.

prewarm_s.description: Simulated seconds rendered before the window opens and not recorded, so every camera's view is ready -- its tiles in, its picture settled -- before the first capture (03 §9.5.1). A view not ready by the window's opening refuses the run; the window is not moved.

world_delta_s.description: Simulated seconds per world tick. The SUMO step must be a whole number of them.

capture_hz.description: Captures per simulated second, on every channel. One capture must be a whole number of world ticks.

road_layer_visible.description: Draw the generated road surface. Hidden by default: it is a flat ribbon over the photogrammetry of the real road, so drawn it is an artefact in every frame.

signal_layer_visible.description: Draw the generated traffic-light and sign meshes. Hidden by default; SUMO simulates the signals either way.

render_set.description: Which vehicles get a body. all (the default): every vehicle SUMO has. The others are optional performance controls -- circle: those inside capture.render_region; cameras: those inside, or about to enter, the ground footprint of any channel's camera, orbits included, with capture.render_region deciding until the cameras are placed where it is given, and every vehicle where it is not. A vehicle a limit leaves out is simulated by SUMO and has no body, no frame and no truth record; the run's record counts it.

render_region.description: The circle vehicles get a body inside, in CARLA's frame (x east, y south, metres): for the whole run under render_set circle, which needs it, and under cameras only until the channels' cameras are placed. Read by no other render set (check 53).

render_hysteresis_m.description: Under render_set circle, how much further out than the region's radius a vehicle keeps its body; under cameras, the band beyond a footprint's widest admission threshold it is kept inside.

render_cap.description: How many vehicles may hold a body at once, under any render set; null (the default) for no limit. Under all, a vehicle drawn keeps its body and a newcomer takes a free place in the scenario seed's order; under circle the nearest the centre are drawn; under cameras a vehicle in view ranks ahead of one approaching, one drawn ahead of a newcomer, then the seed decides.

render_min_pixels.description: Under render_set cameras: a camera's footprint is capped at the range beyond which the catalogue's longest body covers fewer than this many pixels along its length, anywhere in the picture.

render_admit_lead_s.description: Under render_set cameras: simulated seconds of its own travel ahead of a camera's footprint a vehicle is admitted, beyond a margin of its body and one SUMO step, so it appears out of view.

render_release_lag_s.description: Under render_set cameras: simulated seconds a vehicle drawn is held after it last was within reach of a camera's footprint, before it is released.

draw_distance_m.description: An optional performance control, off when null (the default): how far from a camera, in metres, a vehicle's body is drawn. Rendering only: every vehicle keeps its body, its pose and its truth, and a body farther than this from a channel's camera is not in that channel's images, whose sidecars mark it beyond_draw_distance. It must reach the point every channel is aimed at (check 52).

sensor_id.description: The channel's camera's name, such as Overwatch_1 or Southeast_1700m_orbit: 1 to 63 characters, each an ASCII letter, digit, underscore or hyphen, and not a Windows device name (CON, NUL, COM1, ...), a stock sensor role name (front, back, left, right, ...) or CARLA-SENSOR-<number>. Required when there is more than one channel, and unique among them, case aside. It names the channel's capture directory, begins every still's file name (<sensor_id>_<local capture time>) and is the platform track's callsign; refused at pre-roll where a camera in the world already holds it. A single channel without one is named CARLA-SENSOR-<camera actor id>.

pattern.description: stare holds one pose; orbit circles a centre with the view held on it.

orbit_centre_x_m.description: Orbit: the centre it circles, x metres. Required for an orbit.

orbit_centre_y_m.description: Orbit: the centre it circles, y metres (south). Required for an orbit.

orbit_centre_z_m.description: Orbit: the height the altitude is measured from, metres.

orbit_altitude_m.description: Orbit: height above the centre, metres.

stare_look_at_x_m.description: Stare: the point looked at, x metres; with stare_look_at_y_m. Or name stare_look_at_target, or give the five stare pose fields instead.

stare_look_at_y_m.description: Stare: the point looked at, y metres (south).

stare_look_at_z_m.description: Stare: the height of that point, metres. Not used with stare_look_at_target, whose point carries the vehicles' own height.

stare_look_at_target.description: Stare: a point named instead of given. rendered_traffic is the centre of the vehicles the session rendered on the last frame before the camera holds for the window; the camera follows it through the prewarm until one SUMO step and 120 ticks before the window opens (7 s at the defaults), then holds the pose it resolves to while its view becomes ready and for the whole window, and the run result records that point. Needs a prewarm of at least one SUMO step.

stare_altitude_m.description: Stare: height above the point, metres.

stare_standoff_m.description: Stare: horizontal distance back from the point, metres; 0 looks straight down.

stare_bearing_deg.description: Stare: the compass direction the camera looks along, degrees clockwise from north.

stare_x_m.description: Stare pose: x metres; all five pose fields or none.

stare_pitch_deg.description: Stare pose: pitch, degrees; negative looks down.

stare_yaw_deg.description: Stare pose: yaw, degrees; 0 faces east, -90 north.

post_process_profile.description: The post-process profile the camera spawns with, which sets its exposure: Default, GoPro, Town10HD_Opt or Town_C. Named with the file's own case, so it resolves on a case-sensitive file system.

channels.description: The cameras, one object each; see the channel fields below. Every channel is recorded.

enabled.description: Measure per-vehicle occlusion against a depth camera at each stare channel's pose. Session-fixed: turning it off mid-run would change the unoccluded denominator.

margin_m.description: How much nearer than a vehicle's own surface something must be to block it, metres.

samples.description: How finely each vehicle's outline is sampled.

depth_max_range_m.description: The depth camera's range, metres. A surface beyond it reads as sky.

mode.description: as_available: the world ticks as fast as the machine allows. wall_clock: ticks are held to the wall clock at pacing.real_time_factor.

real_time_factor.description: Under wall_clock, simulated seconds per wall-clock second. Not a field under as_available.

min_achieved_factor.description: Under wall_clock, required: the achieved factor below which the prewarm refuses the window and the run is loud. Not a field under as_available.

window_s.description: Wall-clock seconds the achieved factor is measured over.

policy.description: What the sun does across the window: freeze_at_window_start, advance, freeze_at or ignore. The scenario's illumination default supplies it; an override is recorded against the value it replaced.

rate_sun_s_per_sim_s.description: Under advance, pinned to 1.0: one sun-second per simulated second is the only rate under which recorded solar time is the scenario's clock (12 D12.8).

freeze_at_civil_time.description: Under freeze_at, the civil time of day the sun is held at, HH:MM:SS.

freeze_date_advances.description: Under a freeze, whether the sun's date follows the civil date when the epoch's calendar advances.

require_sun.description: Whether a world with no sun refuses the run. Unset means required.

note.description: Why this policy, in one sentence.

allow_version_mismatch.description: Run with a SUMO release other than the one that converted the world, instead of refusing. The session records that it did.

home.description: The SUMO installation to launch, the directory holding bin/sumo. Unset, the session searches SUMO_HOME and then PATH.

timeout_s.description: Seconds to wait for the server to answer a request.

scenario_root.description: Where compiled scenario packages are found by id.

world_package_root.description: Where world packages are found by the name a scenario lock records.

catalogue.description: The measured vehicle catalogue. Its digest must be the scenario lock's.

capture_root.description: Where captures are written, one directory per session and one per channel inside it.

runs_root.description: Where a run's result, resolution report and lock are written by default.

network_fingerprint.description: The canonical fingerprint of the SUMO network the world carries.

opendrive_sha256.description: The digest of the world's OpenDRIVE.

origin_latitude.description: The latitude pinned to the map's origin.

origin_longitude.description: The longitude pinned to the map's origin.

netconvert_version.description: The netconvert that converted the world.

scenario_id.description: The scenario's id, from its lock.

lock_sha256.description: The digest of the scenario lock the run binds.

epoch.description: What simulated second zero means in civil time. A binding: a run that rendered another time would contradict its own scenario (12 D12.9).

sumo_step_s.description: SUMO's step. Never changed to suit the renderer (03 D3.6).

sumo_seed.description: SUMO's seed, compiled into the scenario's configuration.

end_s.description: The simulated second the scenario ends at.

catalogue_digest.description: The digest of the catalogue the scenario was compiled against.

accept_skipped_dry_run.description: Run a scenario whose compile skipped its SUMO-only run (compile_scenario.py --skip-dry-run), or whose lock records none, instead of refusing it (check 54). That run is what finds a vehicle the supervision plan names that never enters the simulation; without it the same fault stops the run only when SUMO drops the vehicle. The echo and the session's report record the acceptance.
